name: Kreisel
prior: Gamechanger Audio Motor Synth / MKII: pitch comes from eight small motors spinning optical discs ('the rate at which the electromotors spin affects the frequencies produced'), per-voice pitch envelope with 'ACCELERATION & BRAKE' controls, i.e. a playable note instrument whose pitch has physical inertia (VS: gamechangeraudio.com/motor-synth-mkii; bhphotovideo.com 1828286; chicagomusicexchange.com blog). Siren Creator (aaddrick, GitHub, MIT): browser siren simulator on AudioWorklet, rotor/stator port rings, 'frequency = ports x RPM / 60', 'Motor dynamics simulate realistic spin-up growl, coast-down, and wail sweeps', motor power and rotor weight controls, 'a toy for my kid', no notes (V: github.com/aaddrick/siren README fetched). DubSiren 2.0 / Tekit DubSiren: siren synths from modulation waveforms, no rotor mass (VS: gearnews.com; tekitaudio.itch.io/dubsiren). Reason Rotor and Klevgrand Spinn: Leslie models where 'the horn ... ramps up and down faster than the drum ... due to the inertia' = effects (VS: bhphotovideo.com reason rotor; soundonsound.com spinn). New Systems Instruments Inertia (Eurorack): a slew/physics module, not a voice (VS: reverb.com 90844297). iOS: siren apps are sample soundboards (Simple Sirens LMT, Air Raid Siren with a hand-siren sample; VS: apps.apple.com). US 12,240,375 B2 (2025): electronically controlled siren where rotor spin speed sets the sound (VS: patentsgazette). Research: hydraulophone siren mechanism (R: synthesis.md 3.11); 'edge-like interaction' (R: musicians.md P1). Not found: a voice in which the note is earned by pumping and a Puls lane's density sets the pitch of a shared rotor.
costNotes: Native: 2 oscillators with a cached 'sirene' PeriodicWave (A.waves, APP 2809) 0.12 + noise BufferSource 0.06 + bandpass 0.06 + precession LFO 0.06 + ~6 gains 0.18 = ~0.48 -> 0.5 at L1 (R: webaudio.md section 4 node costs); L3 three port rows x two sides + two air bands ~1.0. The rotor ODE in tick() (25 ms) is one multiply-add per voice; setTargetAtTime on 3-6 frequency params per tick is cheap and smooth. Budget risk is lifetime, not CPU: a lane voice lives nachlauf (up to 6 s) after the last hit and must be held-type (never stolen, APP 10248), so four Kreisel lanes pin 2-4 units permanently; cap at one rotor per lane and kill at omega < 0.1 omega*.
soundHeld: Simulated (M: ideas/check/sim/perf_krs_sim.js, first-order rotor, steady state = pump x omega*). As written, Hoehe is a pitch control, not air pressure: pump = 0.3 + 0.7 y puts the steady state at -2084 ct (y = 0), -750 ct (y = 0.5) and only at y = 1 on the note; the snap window (30 ct) is reached after 4.1 x traegheit (4.0 s at the default 1 s, 1.2 s at 0.3 s, never within 6 s at 3 s), because a first-order rise spends 4 time constants on the last 1.75 %. Needed: a governor - omega* is the note regardless of y, y only sets torque (rise time) and the air/brass timbre - and a wider catch (snap from 150 ct, i.e. after ~2 T) or a second-order rotor that overshoots and settles. Start from omega = 0 puts the oscillators at 0 Hz (DC, sub-audio thumps): begin at >= 0.15 omega* (a real siren's growl). Then the held note is exactly the promised 'earned' note with a sagging release (-216 ct after 0.25 s, -866 ct after 1 s at nachlauf 2 s; the voice ends after 4.6 s, 18 s at 8 s), and the precession wobble that shrinks as the rotor locks is a lovely detail. Timbre: 10 harmonics at 1/n is a sawtooth (Nebel-adjacent when fast); the identity needs the pulse character of a port disc (narrow pulses, duty from Hoehe) plus the 1.5 omega row and the 8 omega air band - keep those.
soundBurst: Simulated Puls with kicks delta sized so 16ths at 120 bpm (8 Hz) reach the note at nachlauf 2 s: the density-to-pitch law is linear and unbounded - 8 Hz -> -56 ct (the note), 4 Hz -> -1252 ct, 2 Hz -> -2440 ct (two octaves down: a 110 Hz lane hums at 27 Hz), 16 Hz -> +698 ct ABOVE the note; per-hit ripple 158 ct at 8 Hz, 261 at 4 Hz, 468 at 2 Hz (each hit bumps the pitch 1.5-5 semitones, then it sags) - characterful 'Pumpstoss' but uncontrolled, and the lane never plays its note except at one density. Quadratic drag (reib2) compresses it (16 Hz -> note, 8 Hz -> -834 ct, ripple 107 ct). Better law: kicks seek the target, delta = kick x vel x (omega* - omega), plus the governor cap - sparse hits still sit low (the promised 'tief hupen'), dense hits converge on the note and never overshoot, ripple shrinks as the rotor locks. Then the lane is a breathing siren drone whose pitch follows the pattern density and glides between lane notes (portamento by physics) - say in the UI that a Kreisel lane is a drone, not a melody lane; with laneNote changes the rotor glides, which is the siren's charm.
failureModes: Hoehe scales the steady-state pitch (-21 semitones at y = 0, note only at y = 1): add a governor so omega* is the note and y sets torque/timbre
First-order rise reaches the 30 ct snap window only after 4 x traegheit (4 s at default): widen the catch to ~150 ct or use a second-order rotor
Puls density -> pitch is unbounded: 16ths overshoot +700 ct, quarters sit two octaves low (sub-audio on bass lanes); kicks must seek the target and the cap must hold
Per-hit pitch ripple of 1.5-5 semitones (M) is an uncontrolled wobble; target-seeking kicks or quadratic drag
Start at omega = 0 is DC and sub-audio; begin at >= 0.15 omega*
Lane voices live up to nachlauf (6 s; 18 s at reibung 8 s) as held-type voices: four lanes pin 2-4 units; one rotor per lane, strict lifetime
Sawtooth-like 1/n spectrum is Nebel-adjacent when fast; keep the port-disc pulse character, the 1.5 omega row and the air band or it is a glide synth
Keyboard play is always a glide: ship a 'traegheit klein' preset and per-note rotors for chords
verdict: Rare rather than new: pitch with physical inertia is the Gamechanger Motor Synth's whole premise (motors with acceleration/brake, a note instrument), a browser siren with spin-up growl and coast-down exists as a toy (Siren Creator, AudioWorklet, no notes) and dub-siren plugins are LFO toys; unfound is the performer's loop - energy earns the note and Puls density sets the pitch of a rotor that outlives the hits. Native at ~0.5 units (L3 ~1.0) with a trivial tick-rate ODE; the budget risk is lifetime, since lane rotors are held-type voices for up to 6 s. The equations as written break the concept: Hoehe scales the steady state (-21 semitones at y = 0, the note only at y = 1 after 4 s), dense Puls overshoots the note by +700 ct while quarters sit two octaves low, and each hit wobbles the pitch by 1.5-5 semitones - a governor on omega*, target-seeking kicks and a 150 ct catch window fix all three and leave the sagging release and the precession wobble intact. With those it is the most physical idea in the set: a drone siren lane breathing with the pattern and a held note that must be pumped into tune, distinct from Tiefe's fall and from everything else in Myzel.
